subject: Post-demo: top_k behavioral tests, auth matrix, and next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@fastsearch.ai>
Cc: sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: top_k behavioral tests, auth matrix, and next steps

Hi Jordan — thanks again for the product demo earlier today; appreciate you walking us through your relevance goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope the reranker pilot: 

Summary of key needs
- Improve organic search reordering for product pages (reduce incorrect top-3 results)
- Want to preserve latency SLOs: 95th percentile under 120ms for search path
- Need an evaluation strategy that separates relevance regressions from hallucination noise

Technical follow-ups / asks (can you confirm these?):
1) SDK & auth: are you planning to use API keys from our Hosted API or run in a VPC Private deployment? If hosted, do you want OAuth2 with scoped tokens or simple API keys for the pilot? We included an "auth matrix" attachment with options and tradeoffs.
2) Routing: will search traffic be routed through a single rewrite layer today, or do you have multi-region split-routes? We need to know so we can propose cache key strategies.
3) Data for eval: can you share a sample of 1k historical queries with clicked-url labels (CSV) plus a 200-item seed set for behavioral tests? We can run top_k sweeps (k=1,3,5,10) and produce NDCG/precision@k and pairwise swap-rate metrics.
4) Relevance metrics: we propose NDCG@10, precision@3, and a custom "top-3 swap reduction" rate. Do these align with your product goals?

Attached: evaluation rubric (rwrk-eval-rubric.xlsx), auth matrix (auth-matrix.pdf), and a short SDK snippets doc (soojin-sdk-snippets.md) showing auth flows and a minimal rerank call.

Proposed timeline
- This week: you share sample data + confirm auth choice
- Next week: we run a baseline sweep and deliver a short report + recommended top_k default and tuning knobs
- Week after: joint tech call to review results and plan canary rollout

If that looks good, can you confirm: (a) whether you prefer Hosted API (API keys) or Private deployment (mTLS/OAuth), and (b) whether you can share the sample CSV by Thursday PST?

Thanks — I'll loop Marissa for the test harness and Sergio for the rollout/options.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Cc: Legal Ops <procure@fastsearch.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: top_k behavioral tests, auth matrix, and next steps

Thanks Soojin — great summary. Quick answers inline:

On auth: For the pilot we'd prefer Hosted API with scoped API keys — simpler for our infra team. Ultimately we may move to Private for PII-sensitive routes, but pilot = hosted.
On routing: single rewrite layer today (all search traffic from US-east). Cache keys are per-query + user-seg; we can share the routing diagram.
On data: we can export 1,200 queries with clicked-url labels. I'll attach a short sample now and share the full CSV via a secure link by Thursday.
On metrics: NDCG@10 and precision@3 sound right; the custom top-3 swap reduction is interesting — can you define it precisely?

Two quick asks from our side:
- Can Redwood provide a small client-side snippet (Node/Python) showing token refresh flow for scoped API keys?
- We'd like to understand how top_k affects cost. If you can include cost delta estimates for k=1,3,5,10 in the baseline report, helpful for our procurement.

I'll loop in our procurement folks for the pilot paperwork after we see the eval plan.

Best,
Jordan
Product Lead, Search
FastSearch.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@fastsearch.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: top_k behavioral tests, auth matrix, and next steps

Jordan — looping in a few technical details and a concrete plan for the baseline sweep.

Defining the "top-3 swap reduction" metric
- For a given query q, baseline top-3 set = ordered results produced by your current ranking. Redwood reranker top-3 set = ordered results after reranking.
- top-3 swap reduction = 1 - (mean number of inversions between baseline and reranker top-3 that result in a clickable mismatch / mean baseline inversions). Essentially measures how often reranker reduces incorrect high-rank swaps. We'll compute a confidence interval via bootstrap.

Baseline sweep plan
- Candidate k values: 1, 3, 5, 10
- For each k: run reranker across sample queries and compute NDCG@10, precision@3, latency distribution (p50/p95), token delta, and cost delta per 1k queries.
- Behavioral tests: create 6 focused query slices (ambiguous queries, brand queries, long-tail, synonyms, FAQ-answers, shopping-intent) and measure per-slice precision/recall.

Auth snippet and SDK notes
- Attached is a short Node example that demonstrates scoped API key usage + refresh via our token service (see soojin-sdk-snippets.md). For Hosted API pilot: scoped API keys are sufficient; we recommend rotating keys weekly and using per-route scopes.

Cost modeling
- We'll include an estimated token delta and an approximate cost delta for each k using your sample data distribution. Cost numbers will be conservative and labeled as estimates for Hosted pricing.

Next actions from Redwood (this week)
- We will run the baseline sweep as soon as we get the full CSV link and sample routing diagram.
- Deliverable: Baseline report (metrics, plots, recommended default k, and cost delta) within 3 business days after data receipt.

Marissa
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: node-scoped-key-sample.js (application/javascript)]
